full_judgment: 12. In dismissing the suit learned Judge found admitted fact that there is no deed of Waqf to enroll the property as waqf property but for long uses although there is no deed of Waqf, the property has attained the character of Waqf property and in arriving such finding, learned Judge considered section 188 of Molla's Mohammadan law and also relied on the decision reported in 152 I.C. 50 wherein it is held that "Where for a number of years prayers were offered by the public in a mosque close by a tomp of a Mohammedian saint, and an annual 'Uras' attended by Mohammedians of 11)Tomin' sect had been regularly held, the mosque and the tamp must be presumed to have been duly dedicated and to have become waqf by user and this presumption might fairly be extended to other buildings and lands enclosed within the compound wall which might be regarded as appurtenant to the tomp." According to the aforesaid decision the land of Dargah of Hazrat Shah Jalal waqf land. Learned Judge also took the view that plaintiffs did not produce any document to show that defendant No. 4 E not Mutwalli of Dargah Hazrat Shah Jalal and has no authority to enlist this property as waqf property and was of the opinion that if the property be not waqf property then defendant No.4 could not deterrent of his own interest enlisted the property as waqf property. Learned Judge also found that later on, defendant No. 4 applied to defendant No. 1 for enlistment of the suit property as waqf property and notice was served upon plaintiff No. I but plaintiff  No. I could not produce any paper to show that he raised any objection. Thereafter, learned Judge hold on reference to section 94 (I) (Ka) of Waqf. Ordinance, 1962 and also section 4 of the Waqf Ordinance, Ordinance XII of 1966 i.e. East Pakistan. Waqf Ordinance, 1966 the property is a public waqf. Learned Judge also considered as per section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 the Administrator who decide whether the property is waqf or not took into consideration the judgment and decree passed by the learned District Judge as exhibit 3(G) and 3 (H) and held that as per section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance. 1962 the property is waqf property.
